overview.goal: Identify and eliminate the primary causes of sluggish GUI and WebGL performance, then incrementally apply high-impact rendering and architecture improvements.
priority_order: Replace full-scene scans with spatial indexing
Reduce GPU overdraw and postprocessing cost
Adopt scalable rendering and picking strategies

telemetry_strategy.purpose: Capture long-lived performance data in a format that is compact, searchable, and cheap to inspect without loading excessive context.
design_principles: Prefer structured events over free-form logs.
Use small numeric fields and short enumerations instead of verbose text.
Store aggregated session summaries separately from raw samples.
Keep hot-path telemetry write operations non-blocking.
Support line-oriented or record-oriented lookup for fast agent analysis.

recommended_storage_model.primary_store: append-only JSONL or SQLite-style event store
recommended_storage_model.access_pattern: query by event type, session id, timestamp range, and object id
agent_read_optimization: fixed schema with stable field names
small payloads with optional detail blocks

retention_policy.raw_samples: short retention, sampled or ring-buffered for debugging
thresholds: log only frames above a defined cost threshold in detail
sample normal frames at a lower rate

sections.title: Profile first
sections.summary: Measure React, render, and interaction hotspots before changing architecture.
tasks: Capture React commit duration during drag/select/link operations.
Measure frame time during camera movement and shape dragging.
Count store writes per second from camera and pointer sync paths.
Measure raycasts and pointer-related work per frame.
Count draw calls and postprocessing cost at typical scene sizes.
Emit structured telemetry events for interaction start, interaction end, and frame spikes.
Record summarized performance sessions with timestamps, scene size, and hotspot tags.
Persist telemetry in a compact, queryable store optimized for fast inspection by type, session, and time range.
verification_steps: Confirm the app maintains stable frame time under interaction.
Record baseline performance metrics for comparison after each optimization.
Verify profiling traces identify the heaviest components and render paths.
Confirm telemetry events can be queried by event_kind and session_id without scanning full logs.
Verify summary records expose p95 frame time, max frame time, and hotspot labels.
Confirm stored samples remain compact enough to inspect quickly in-line or by targeted lookup.
debug_steps: Use browser performance profiling to isolate long tasks on the main thread.
Inspect flame charts for repeated renders caused by store updates.
Log interaction frequency and frame-related updates to correlate spikes with user actions.
Query only the relevant telemetry slices for a given session, event kind, or entity.
Use compact summaries first, then drill into raw events only for the hottest ranges.
If telemetry volume becomes noisy, lower the sampling rate for normal frames while preserving spikes.

sections.title: Fix the biggest UI-thread offenders
sections.summary: Remove the most expensive per-frame and per-interaction JavaScript work.
tasks: Throttle or eliminate camera-to-store sync on every frame.
Replace full deep-clone history snapshots with patch-based or delta-based history.
Use spatial indexing for collision checks and placement validation.
Reduce placement indicator work to pointer-change-driven updates.
Minimize DOM overlay and animation work inside the canvas.
verification_steps: Dragging shapes should no longer trigger obvious UI stalls.
Undo and redo should remain responsive as scene size grows.
Placement should stay smooth with many objects on the canvas.
Pointer movement should not generate unnecessary React rerenders.
debug_steps: Compare render counts before and after store throttling.
Measure memory allocations during repeated undo/redo operations.
Trace collision queries to confirm spatial lookup replaces full-array scans.

sections.title: Optimize rendering
sections.summary: Reduce draw cost, overdraw, and expensive scene recomposition.
tasks: Batch repeated scene elements such as ports, handles, and selection markers.
Avoid unnecessary recomputation of bounds and geometry-derived values.
Reduce transparent layers and expensive compositing where possible.
Make postprocessing adaptive based on interaction state and device capability.
Use level-of-detail behavior based on zoom and visibility.
verification_steps: Draw call count should decrease after batching and instancing improvements.
GPU time should drop when postprocessing is reduced during interaction.
The scene should remain visually correct at low and high zoom levels.
debug_steps: Use renderer statistics to compare draw calls before and after batching.
Measure GPU frame time with postprocessing enabled and disabled.
Verify no visual artifacts appear when LOD or reduced effects are active.

sections.title: Scale architecture
sections.summary: Separate fast-changing simulation state from persistent UI state and prepare for growth.
tasks: Split hot interaction state from cold persisted scene state.
Move simulation-style updates to refs or non-React controllers where appropriate.
Use workers for expensive layout, overlap, and routing calculations.
Introduce scene-level culling and zoom-aware rendering paths.
Add GPU picking or ID-buffer selection for dense scenes.
verification_steps: Interaction should remain smooth as the scene reaches higher object counts.
Worker-based computations should not block pointer or camera responsiveness.
Selection accuracy should remain correct after switching to GPU-assisted picking.
debug_steps: Confirm hot state changes no longer cause broad component rerenders.
Profile main-thread time before and after worker offloading.
Validate picking correctness against known object IDs and edge cases.

sections.title: Implementation sequencing
sections.summary: Apply the plan in a controlled order to minimize regression risk.
tasks: Complete profiling and establish baseline metrics.
Apply the highest-impact low-risk fixes first.
Re-profile after each change set.
Only then proceed to batching, culling, and GPU-driven enhancements.
Keep a changelog of what improved, what regressed, and what remains open.
verification_steps: Each change set should have a before/after performance comparison.
The app should remain functionally correct after each milestone.
Regression checks should confirm editing, linking, undo/redo, and selection still work.
debug_steps: If a change worsens performance, revert it and isolate the cause with profiling.
Track regressions separately for CPU, GPU, and interaction latency.
Use focused tests or manual scenarios for drag, zoom, select, and link workflows.

notes: This plan is intentionally iterative and should be updated as measurements are collected.
Mark a section complete only after verification steps pass and the improvement is visible in profiling.
Keep the plan in sync with code changes so it remains the source of truth for optimization work.
Telemetry should remain compact, queryable, and session-oriented so future analysis can target only the relevant records.
